prompt.context: Our client, ML Bank, is the 5th largest bank in North America in terms of number of branch locations, with over $20B in revenue in 2015. They've grown to this size through years of inorganic growth, with several acquisitions within the past few years. They've recently engaged a consulting firm to conduct a benchmarking study which revealed their costs are over-market by $400M. They've hired you to identify and fix the underlying cause of this discrepancy.
prompt.question: Identify and fix the underlying cause of why ML Bank's costs are $400M over-market.

clarifying_info.q: What type of banking does ML Bank focus on and where are their branches?
clarifying_info.a: ML Bank focuses on retail banking and has over 1,000 locations throughout the Northeastern US and Canada.

clarifying_info.q: What types of companies has ML Bank acquired?
clarifying_info.a: Most of their acquisitions have been mid-size banks in the Northeastern US and regional credit card portfolios.

clarifying_info.q: How are profits trending despite the cost discrepancy?
clarifying_info.a: Profits have remained steady despite the cost discrepancy.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other goals beyond cost reduction?
clarifying_info.a: Assume there are no other goals that the bank has at this time other than to reduce costs.

exhibits.title: Costs
exhibits.shows: A table and legend showing ML Bank's cost breakdown by category for 2014 and 2015 (in $ millions), alongside the 2015 industry average percentage for each category.

exhibits.title: High-Cost Systems
exhibits.shows: A table listing six IT systems at ML Bank, with columns for System Name, System Function, Age of System (Years), System Business Need, Customers Supported, Annual Cost (Millions), and Time to Transition (years). The CTO has identified these as high cost-drivers prime for removal.

footnotes.business_need: Rough determination of how the system aligns with overall future business strategy.
footnotes.time_to_transition: Estimate of how long it would take to transition from this system to a new one.

framework: Identify whether this is a cost, revenue, or profit problem — it is a cost problem; profits are steady
Structure costs MECE: Salaries & Benefits, Interest Expense, Branches & Equipment, Technology, Provision for Credit Losses, Compliance/Taxes, Other Expenses
Compare each cost category YoY (2014 vs 2015) and vs. 2015 industry average to isolate the anomaly
Hypothesize root cause — link cost spike to recent inorganic growth / acquisitions
Quantify the gap and evaluate options to close it
Recommend specific actions, assess risks, and outline next steps

questions.prompt: Analyze Exhibit 1: which cost category is driving costs over-market, and by how much?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare 2015 ML Bank percentages to 2015 industry averages and also calculate YoY change. Technology stands out: it rose 175% YoY (from $500M in 2014 to $1,375M in 2015), jumped from 3% to 10% of total costs, vs. an industry average of only 2%. All other categories are roughly in line with industry averages. A complete answer also notes that total costs grew from $14,450M to $15,415M (+$965M), and that Technology alone accounts for $875M of that increase.

math.setup: Compare each cost line as % of total costs in 2014, 2015, and vs. industry average. Calculate YoY % change for Technology.
steps: Other categories all within ~1-2pp of industry average
math.answer: Technology costs increased 175% YoY and represent ~10% of total costs vs. a 2% industry average, making Technology the primary driver of ML Bank's above-market costs.

questions.prompt: What are potential reasons for the large increase in technology expenditures?
questions.guidance: A good answer links the spike to ML Bank's recent acquisitions. Acquiring mid-size banks and regional credit card portfolios brings entire technology portfolios: IT applications, software licenses, IT staff, data centers, servers, and customer-facing channels (websites, web apps, call centers). Mergers create bloated, duplicative IT portfolios. A great answer also suggests remedies such as application rationalization, eliminating redundant systems, and streamlining. Technology consulting candidates should also mention: Application Rationalization and Standardization, ERP Implementation, Storage/Server/Data Center Optimization, Mainframe consolidation, LAN/WAN/Voice and Data Network Optimization, PC Management, and Maintenance/Help Desk Outsourcing, all aligned to a People-Processes-Technology framework.

questions.prompt: The CTO wants a 17.5% reduction in technology costs over the next two years. Using Exhibit 2, which systems should ML Bank retire to achieve this goal?
questions.guidance: Candidate must first calculate the target savings, then evaluate each system on Business Need, duplication, cost, and transition time. AIMS (Low business need, $100M cost) and HRIS-1 (duplicate HR function vs. BHRIMS, Medium vs. High business need, $150M cost) are the recommended retirements. Combined savings of $250M exceed the $240M target. Candidate should talk through each column qualitatively before making a selection.

steps: AIMS annual cost = $100M; Business Need = Low; no customers supported
HRIS-1 annual cost = $150M; Business Need = Medium; duplicates BHRIMS (also HR Management, High need); no customers supported
math.answer: Retire AIMS and HRIS-1 for combined annual savings of $250M, exceeding the $240M (17.5%) target. This also begins to close the $400M over-market cost gap identified in the benchmarking study.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some potential reasons for the large increase in technology expenditures at ML Bank?

categories.name: Acquisition-driven bloat
ideas: Inherited full IT portfolios from acquired banks and credit card companies
Duplicate applications performing the same function (e.g., two HR systems)
Multiple data centers and server farms
Duplicate IT staff and support teams

categories.name: Customer-facing technology duplication
ideas: Multiple websites/web portals from different legacy banks

categories.name: Legacy and aging systems
ideas: Old systems with expensive maintenance contracts
Systems no longer aligned with business strategy but not yet retired
High cost to maintain mainframe-based legacy infrastructure

categories.name: Integration and migration costs
ideas: Ongoing costs to integrate acquired systems
Failed or delayed integration projects consuming budget

categories.name: Compliance and security overhead
ideas: Each acquired entity brought its own compliance/security tech stack

recommendation: Retire AIMS (Internal Accounting, Low business need, $100M/year) and HRIS-1 (HR Management duplicate of BHRIMS, Medium business need, $150M/year) to achieve $250M in annual technology cost savings.

This exceeds the CTO's 17.5% (~$240M) reduction target and meaningfully closes the $400M over-market cost gap identified in the benchmarking study, though further rationalization may be needed to fully close the gap.
risks: Loss of business continuity if systems are retired without adequate migration planning
Data migration complexity and risk when moving from AIMS to the retained accounting platform
Contractual software license costs may continue for the duration of the contract even after retirement decision
Transition periods (1 year for AIMS, 1.5 years for HRIS-1) mean savings are not immediate
Employee disruption and change management challenges from HR system consolidation
next_steps: Scope the full data migration and integration requirements for retiring AIMS and HRIS-1
Identify and confirm the target-state IT application portfolio (application rationalization roadmap)
Map out a phased sunset roadmap with milestones to ensure business continuity
Conduct a broader review of the remaining IT portfolio for further rationalization opportunities to fully close the $400M cost gap
Align the technology strategy with overall business strategy using a People-Processes-Technology framework (especially relevant for Technology Consulting roles)
